title: Why the Himalayas Are Still Rising
meta_description: Understand how the Indian and Eurasian plates continue to converge, building Himalayan mountains while earthquakes, erosion, and landslides reshape them.
h1: Why The Himalayas Are Still Rising?
author: Suraj Dahal
key_takeaways: The Himalayas formed as the Indian plate moved north and collided with Eurasia tens of millions of years ago.
Convergence continues today, shortening and thickening crust and loading major faults; the movement is not a uniform upward elevator across every peak.
Rock uplift, surface uplift and changes in elevation are related but not identical: erosion can remove material even while tectonic forces push rock upward.
The active plate boundary produces damaging earthquakes, and steep terrain, monsoon rainfall, glaciers and rivers also shape Himalayan landscapes.
